wa_lower_cheeks.blurb: Lower Cheeks is the bottom portion of the big pale Cheeks formation on the upper walls above the town of Index, in the Skykomish Valley off Highway 2. About two thirds of the roughly thirty routes are trad, with a handful of bolted lines and one aid climb, and the grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11 with a few 5.12 and 5.13 testpieces and only a couple of easier options. The granite is steep, and some lines stay dry through light rain. A wide ledge at mid-height, reachable by a fixed cable, makes this one of the better spots at Index for setting up top ropes. Expect a hike of around forty minutes from the car.

wa_powerline_wall_west.blurb: Powerline Wall West is the western end of a popular wall on Mount Erie, a short drive south of Anacortes on Fidalgo Island. Most of the thirty-one climbs are bolted sport lines, with a smaller number of trad routes, and the grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.11, with the largest group in the 5.10 range. Access is quick: you arrive at the cliff top from the summit area, walk along the rim, and scramble down a low third-class ramp to the base. The wall faces the afternoon sun, so it can feel pleasant on clear winter days. Rock quality is generally good.
wa_powerline_wall_west.approach: From the summit parking area, follow the trail west and under the power lines to the cliff top. Walk along the top to the descent ramp, a low third-class scramble to the base, then turn left for the first bolted lines.

wa_k_9_crag.blurb: K-9 Crag is one of the walls at Fun Rock, the local sport climbing area up Lost River Road from Mazama in the Methow Valley. All thirty-one routes are bolted, and the grades skew hard compared with the rest of the area: a few 5.8 and 5.9 warmups, then a big cluster of 5.11 and 5.12 lines, with a few 5.13s. It is the place to head here when the easier walls feel too mellow. All the Fun Rock walls share a single signed lot, so you can combine it with moderate climbs elsewhere. Pack out trash, and do not camp at the lot.
wa_k_9_crag.parking_note: Use the large signed climbers' lot on Lost River Road, roughly a mile and a half northwest of the Mazama store. Every wall at Fun Rock, including this one, is reached from that single lot.

wv_2_bridge_buttress.blurb: 2 Bridge Buttress sits in the Bridge Area of the New River Gorge near Fayetteville, right beside the road, which makes it one of the most visited cliffs in the national park. Of the forty-nine routes we list, about three quarters are trad and the rest sport, spread from 5.5 up to a few 5.13s, with the heaviest concentration between 5.10 and 5.12. Big roofs give the cliff a steep, powerful feel. Heavy traffic has caused erosion, so stone stairs and belay platforms have been built; stay on the trails. Expect company, especially from newer climbers and guided groups. Drones are not allowed in the park.
